source: JPL Horizons API v1.2 (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api), fetched 2026-08-15; ephemeris DE441; EPHEM_TYPE=OBSERVER, QUANTITIES=4,20, APPARENT=AIRLESS, ANG_FORMAT=DEG

geocentric.ra_dec_note: moon_ra_deg/moon_dec_deg are astrometric ICRF (J2000, light-time only); *_apparent_* are airless apparent, Earth true equator & equinox of date (light-time + light deflection + stellar aberration + precession + nutation)

conventions: Verified from Horizons output headers/footnotes fetched 2026-08-15. (1) Azimuth: 'Azimuth is measured clockwise from north: North(0) -> East(90) -> South(180) -> West(270) -> North(360)'. Elevation is relative to the plane perpendicular to the local zenith of the reference surface (airless apparent, 'a-app': compensated for light-time, gravitational light deflection, stellar aberration, precession and nutation). (2) Lunar topocentric site frame: 'Center pole/equ : MEAN_ME (high precision) {East-longitude positive}' -- i.e. the Moon MEAN-EARTH/polar-axis frame, NOT the principal-axis (PA) frame. (3) SITE_COORD longitude for the Moon is EAST-positive: header echoes 'Center geodetic : 23.4731, .6741, ... {E-lon(deg),Lat(deg),Alt(km)}', and Site B input -68.6 was echoed as 291.4 E-lon, confirming negative input = west longitude. (4) Geocentric Moon table: astrometric RA/DEC are in the ICRF (J2000) frame; apparent RA/DEC are Earth true-equator-and-equinox of date. Sub-observer (sub-Earth) and sub-solar lon/lat on the Moon are planetodetic in the MOON_ME frame ('Target pole/equ : MOON_ME {East-longitude positive}'), light-time corrected, positive longitude EAST. (5) Range 'delta' is apparent (light-time aberrated) distance to target center in au; 'deldot' in km/s. (6) Times are UTC ('Date__(UT)').
